verses.english: “Mendicants, there are four ways of practice.
pleasant practice with slow insight, and

verses.pali: Tatra, bhikkhave, yāyaṁ paṭipadā dukkhā dandhābhiññā, ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭipadā ubhayeneva hīnā akkhāyati. Yampāyaṁ paṭipadā dukkhā, imināpāyaṁ hīnā akkhāyati; yampāyaṁ paṭipadā dandhā, imināpāyaṁ hīnā akkhāyati.
verses.english: Of these, the painful practice with slow insight is said to be inferior in both ways: because it’s painful and because it’s slow.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭipadā ubhayeneva hīnā akkhāyati.
verses.english: This practice is said to be inferior in both ways.

verses.pali: Tatra, bhikkhave, yāyaṁ paṭipadā dukkhā khippābhiññā, ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭipadā dukkhattā hīnā akkhāyati.
verses.english: The painful practice with swift insight is said to be inferior because it’s painful.

verses.pali: Tatra, bhikkhave, yāyaṁ paṭipadā sukhā dandhābhiññā, ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭipadā dandhattā hīnā akkhāyati.
verses.english: The pleasant practice with slow insight is said to be inferior because it’s slow.

verses.pali: Tatra, bhikkhave, yāyaṁ paṭipadā sukhā khippābhiññā, ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭipadā ubhayeneva paṇītā akkhāyati. Yampāyaṁ paṭipadā sukhā, imināpāyaṁ paṇītā akkhāyati; yampāyaṁ paṭipadā khippā, imināpāyaṁ paṇītā akkhāyati.
verses.english: The pleasant practice with swift insight is said to be superior in both ways: because it’s pleasant, and because it’s swift.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭipadā ubhayeneva paṇītā akkhāyati.
verses.english: This practice is said to be superior in both ways.
These are the four ways of practice.”
